Yes we know heat damages our expensive investments/toys, so we have to cool these processors with fans, and RGB. People hardly think about cooling, they just slap on whatever cooler has good reviews on whatever corporate electronics boutique they frequent. They figure more is better, but no one really understands how to get the most performance out of your cooling setup. Mostly because people don't really understand the nature of airflow, and it's properties. Most of the press/youtubers/influencers/whateverthefucks merely gloss over positive pressure, or negative pressure. One thing that seems to crop up over and over again is how good a pull setup is with regards to temperatures, that is negative pressure setup seems to have the overall best performance. We see the data, but no one ever questions why this is so.

If we paid attention in our educational years, or beyond we know about the Bernoulli principle, and the ideal gas laws. Particularly that pressure, temperature, and volume are all inextricably connected. In a sealed container, if the pressure and volume increase, then so does temperature, the inverse is also true. If you lower the pressure, both temperature and volume decrease. In turbocharged cars, intercoolers are used to lower the temperature, and volume of the compressed air, they lower the temperature and volume by creating a pressure drop across the core. This pressure drop lowers the temperature, much like it happens in water cooling.

How does this tie in to airflow and cooling you ask? Well if you have a fan controller and an equal amount of fans you can tune the system to have absolute best performance by exhausting more air than you intake. Similarly on a CPU cooler, a push pull fan setup will be vastly more efficient and effective at removing heat by having the pull fan do most of the work, and the push fan only a small portion, instead of having both fans working at identical duty cycles.
